THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FIX IN THE SYSTEM: it turns a daily loop that already names the owner's best
prospects into actual funnel inflow.

READ FIRST (do not guess the shapes):
  episodes/_loop_receipts/guest-acquisition-20260731.md  — the real receipt. Note its structure:
      a "### 2. A1 candidate intake" section with a numbered list "N. Name: free-text note",
      a "### 3. A2 fit scores" markdown TABLE with columns Candidate | Fit | angle | Confidence,
      and a "Suppressed or parked:" sentence naming people who must NOT be admitted.
  server/pipeline/candidate_ingest.py — the consumer. Match its candidate-inbox-v1 schema EXACTLY
      (schema key, candidates list, per-candidate fields it reads). Do not invent fields it ignores.

BUILD scripts/acquisition_bridge.py:
  parse_acquisition_receipt(text) -> dict
      Pure, stdlib only. Returns {"candidates": [...], "suppressed": [names], "problems": [...]}.
      A candidate carries: name, note (the free text after the name), fit_score (int|None from the A2
      table), confidence (int|None), source ("guest-acquisition-receipt"), evidence (the receipt
      filename + section). Match names between the intake list and the fit table by normalized name
      (casefold, strip punctuation/titles); a candidate present in one but not the other is still
      emitted, with the missing field None and a recorded problem — never dropped silently.
      Anyone in the "Suppressed or parked" sentence is EXCLUDED from candidates and listed in
      "suppressed". A person whose identity the receipt itself marks unverified (the receipt says
      "spelling and surname unverified" / "identity ... unverified") is excluded too, with the reason
      recorded — an unverified identity must never become an outreach target.
      No email addresses appear in these receipts; emit email None and let downstream handle it.
  merge_into_inbox(existing_inbox, parsed, *, now) -> dict
      Returns a NEW candidate-inbox-v1 document. Existing entries are preserved and never duplicated
      (match on normalized name); an existing entry gets its fit_score/note REFRESHED from the newer
      receipt but keeps its original first_seen. New entries get first_seen from `now`. Deterministic
      ordering (fit_score desc, then name).
  main(): --receipt (path, default: newest guest-acquisition-*.md under episodes/_loop_receipts),
      --inbox (default episodes/CANDIDATE-INBOX.json), --apply (DRY RUN BY DEFAULT — print the diff
      summary and write nothing without it). Exit 0 on success, 1 when the receipt cannot be parsed
      into at least one candidate (a silent empty bridge is the failure this exists to prevent),
      2 on unreadable input.

TESTS (tests/test_acquisition_bridge.py; at least 7). Use a REALISTIC receipt fixture built from the
structure described above (write the fixture text inline in the test):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: parsing a receipt with the intake list + fit table yields candidates with names and
     fit scores joined correctly (assert Bryan-style 92 lands on the right person);
 (2) NEGATIVE: a suppressed/parked person in the intake list is NOT a candidate and IS in "suppressed";
 (3) NEGATIVE: a candidate the receipt marks identity-unverified is excluded with a recorded reason;
 (4) merge preserves an existing entry's first_seen while refreshing its fit_score, and does not
     duplicate it;
 (5) NEGATIVE: a receipt with no parseable candidates makes main() exit 1 and write nothing;
 (6) NEGATIVE: dry run (no --apply) writes NOTHING — assert the inbox file is unchanged/absent;
 (7) the emitted document validates against candidate_ingest's reader: feed it through
     candidate_ingest.load_candidate_feed and assert the candidates come back (this is the wire that
     was missing; prove it end to end);
 (8) determinism: same receipt + same now -> identical document including order.
Keep tests/test_candidate_feed_wiring.py green.

THE OWNER'S QUESTION this answers: "how do we see our heijunka board for scheduling?" He must see, in
five seconds on a phone-width terminal, which upcoming Thursdays are EMPTY and where the bottleneck is.

READ FIRST: scripts/funnel_status.py (its build_report and --json structure are your input contract —
reuse it, do not re-implement the aggregation), server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py (the real stage sets).

BUILD scripts/heijunka_board.py — a LEVELING view, not a to-do list:
  thursday_slots(now, count=6) -> [dates]  — the takt grid, next `count` Thursdays from `now`.
  build_board(report, *, now, vps_schedule=None) -> dict
      `report` is the funnel_status JSON structure. `vps_schedule` is an OPTIONAL list of
      {"episode_id","publish_date"} read from a snapshot file (--vps-schedule PATH); when it is None the
      board must SAY SO in its output ("production schedule not supplied — slots shown from local state,
      which is not the publisher"). This warning is mandatory: local certification does not claim a slot.
      SLOT-CLAIM RULE: a Thursday is "filled" only by an episode scheduled in vps_schedule when it is
      supplied; otherwise by local publish_date and the board is marked unverified.
      LANES, grouped from the real stage sets: OUTREACH, PREP/BOOK, RECORDED, PRODUCE, CERTIFY/QUEUE.
      WIP CAPS (derive nothing, use these): OUTREACH 4, PREP/BOOK 3, PRODUCE 3, CERTIFY/QUEUE 2. A lane
      over its cap is the BOTTLENECK and must be flagged.
      COUNTING RULE (this is what made the old number a fiction): an episode counts as in-flight only if
      it has evidence of real work AND no publish receipt. Use episode_evidence/publish_status to decide;
      an episode already published NEVER counts as inventory, and a scaffold with nothing but
      episode.json counts as OUTREACH-stage inventory at most, flagged "scaffold".
      COVER: weeks_of_cover = number of future slots filled (both solo and guest count — the owner runs a
      MIX). Separately compute guest_cover = guest episodes with a booked recording date, because a solo
      takes ~1 week to produce and a guest ~8: a healthy slot count made entirely of solos is a guest
      drought, and the board must show both numbers side by side.
      Returns {"slots": [{date, filled, episode_id|None, kind: guest|solo|None, source}],
               "lanes": [{name, count, cap, over}], "cover_weeks", "guest_cover_weeks",
               "aging": [{episode_id, days_idle}], "warnings": [...]}
  Default output: a compact terminal board — the 6-slot grid one line per slot (EMPTY rows must be
  visually obvious), then lanes with count/cap, then the two cover numbers, then aging and warnings.
  --json emits the structure. Exit 2 when any of the next 2 slots is empty or a lane is over cap
  (so cron can alarm), 0 otherwise. Never write any file.

TESTS (tests/test_heijunka_board.py; at least 7, fixed `now`, synthetic report structures):
 (1) six slots starting from the next Thursday, correct dates, regardless of what weekday `now` is;
 (2) THE REAL CASE: a report whose only future episode is one solo -> exactly one slot filled, five
     EMPTY, cover_weeks 1, guest_cover_weeks 0, exit 2;
 (3) NEGATIVE: with no vps_schedule the board emits the "not the publisher" warning; with one supplied,
     the warning is gone and slots come from it (assert a local-only episode does NOT claim a slot);
 (4) NEGATIVE: an already-published episode never counts as inventory in any lane;
 (5) NEGATIVE: a scaffold episode (only episode.json, no work evidence) is flagged scaffold and does not
     inflate PRODUCE/CERTIFY;
 (6) a lane over its cap is flagged as the bottleneck and forces exit 2;
 (7) guest/solo mix: 3 solos + 1 guest -> cover_weeks 4, guest_cover_weeks reflects only the guest;
 (8) determinism, and the script writes no files (assert the fixture tree is unchanged).

THE DEFECT: queue_status counts WIP and nothing else. It reported "8 episodes are moving, meeting the
target of 6; no new outreach" on a day when the publishing machine had ZERO episodes scheduled and ZERO
guest recordings booked. The alarm threshold (escalate below 3) would not have fired until early
September, and with an ~8-week guest lead time that guarantees a multi-week outage. The metric is not
late; it is measuring a fiction.

THE FIX, inside pipeline_queue.py (keep every existing public function working — other modules and the
funnel/board scripts import them):
1. Add weeks_of_cover(episodes, *, now, takt_per_week=1) -> dict returning
   {"slot_cover_weeks": int, "guest_cover_weeks": int, "slots_at_risk": [dates], "assumptions": [...]}.
   * slot_cover counts FUTURE publishable inventory of ANY kind (solo and guest both — the owner runs a
     mix; this is his 2026-07-31 decision) divided by takt.
   * guest_cover counts only guest episodes with a booked recording date, because guests carry the ~8
     week lead time and a slot count made entirely of solos is a guest drought that must stay visible.
   * An episode that is already published is NEVER inventory. Take that from publish evidence, not from
     the stage string — 4 published episodes counted as "moving" because their local stage lagged.
   * Every estimate that rests on the lead-time or survival assumptions must be named in "assumptions";
     unmeasured is never silently treated as known.
2. Add cover_alarm(episodes, *, now) -> {"level": "ok"|"warn"|"red", "reasons": [...]} with these rules
   (constants named and commented with the 2026-07-31 incident):
     RED when slot_cover_weeks < 2 (a solo can be produced in ~1 week, so under 2 weeks there is no
       recovery room), or when guest_cover_weeks == 0 (no guest is booked to record at all — today's
       true state), or when either of the next 2 Thursdays has nothing publishable.
     WARN when slot_cover_weeks < 4 or guest_cover_weeks < 10 (the ~8 week guest lead time plus 2
       weeks of safety).
     OK otherwise. Unknown/unparseable inputs resolve toward RED, never toward OK — fail closed.
3. queue_status keeps its existing keys (callers depend on them) and gains "cover" (the weeks_of_cover
   dict) and "alarm" (the cover_alarm dict). Do NOT change TARGET_IN_FLIGHT or the existing count
   semantics in this lane — a second lane owns the board; here the job is that the alarm stops lying.

TESTS (tests/test_cover_alarm.py; at least 7, fixed `now`):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: today's shape — several already-published episodes plus three future solos and zero
     booked guest recordings -> slot_cover 3, guest_cover 0, alarm RED naming the guest drought;
 (2) NEGATIVE: an already-published episode never contributes to either cover number;
 (3) a healthy mix (4 future slots incl. 2 booked guests) -> alarm ok or warn, never red;
 (4) NEGATIVE: next-2-Thursdays empty forces RED even when the far-future count looks fine;
 (5) NEGATIVE: an unparseable publish_date resolves toward RED, never OK (fail closed);
 (6) guest_cover_weeks < 10 with slot cover fine -> WARN, and the reason names the lead time;
 (7) assumptions list is non-empty whenever a lead-time-dependent number is reported;
 (8) queue_status still returns every pre-existing key (assert them explicitly so no caller breaks).

THE DEFECT, found by an independent reviewer and confirmed on live data: audit_run labels EVERY
incomplete required step a "silent skip", whether or not the episode has reached that step. A solo
episode booked for a recording three weeks from now reports 23 silent skips — transcription, publishing,
the launch email, referral follow-up. Nothing was skipped; none of it is due. The department supervisor
turns any non-empty silent-skip list into a CRITICAL incident, so the owner now has 43 open decisions and
an alarm he is being trained to ignore. An alarm that fires on normal future work is worse than no alarm.

THE FIX — the discrimination rule (implement exactly this semantics):
  a step is a SILENT SKIP only when it is incomplete AND has no valid skip artifact AND at least one of:
    * a downstream dependent step already completed (the pipeline demonstrably moved past it), or
    * the episode has crossed the stage at which that step was due, or
    * the step carries an explicit due_at that has passed beyond a grace period.
  Everything else is classified, not alarmed: PENDING (upstream not done yet), NOT_DUE (the episode has
  not reached this step's stage), or BLOCKED (an upstream requirement is itself incomplete).

1. Add a per-step notion of the stage by which it is due. Read the real stage vocabulary from
   server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py (_IN_FLIGHT_STAGES / _GUEST_DONE_STAGES / _PUBLISHED_STAGES) and map
   each EPISODE_DAG step to the stage that implies it should have happened. Where a step genuinely has no
   stage mapping, it is NOT_DUE until a downstream step completes — never guessed into alarming.
2. audit_run gains the classification: keep "silent_skips" as the ALARMING set (now narrowed), and add
   "pending", "not_due", "blocked" lists. "complete" stays False only for real silent skips and invalid
   skip artifacts — an episode legitimately mid-flight is not "incomplete" in the alarming sense; add a
   separate boolean like "in_progress" so a consumer can tell the two apart.
3. Existing callers must keep working: the projection export and the done-gate read audit_run's shape.
   Do not remove keys; add. The existing suites are in the verify command and must stay green.

TESTS (tests/test_skip_discrimination.py; at least 6):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: an episode at stage recording-booked with nothing done reports ZERO silent skips and
     puts publishing/launch-email/referral steps in not_due — the 23-alarm case is closed;
 (2) NEGATIVE, the case that MUST still alarm: a downstream step completed while a required upstream one
     never ran (the guest_assets incident) -> silent skip, complete False;
 (3) NEGATIVE: an episode that crossed a step's due stage without doing it -> silent skip;
 (4) a valid skip artifact keeps a due step out of the alarming set (authorized, named);
 (5) NEGATIVE: an invalid/tampered skip artifact still blocks — forged authorization never counts;
 (6) blocked vs pending are distinguished (an upstream-incomplete step is blocked, not pending);
 (7) every EPISODE_DAG step has a due-stage mapping or an explicit no-mapping marker (assert coverage so
     a future step cannot be added without a decision).
Keep tests/test_episode_dag.py, tests/test_skip_artifacts.py and
tests/test_done_gate_and_skip_recording.py green.
